summary: The PWA manifest/service-worker scaffolding (src/app/manifest.ts, public/sw.js, ServiceWorkerRegister.tsx) is sound, correctly bypasses /api/* from the cache, and the disclosed photo-upload gap is genuinely handled honestly with real, non-silent UI and unit tests against fake-indexeddb. However, the offline work-progress queue (src/lib/offline/work-progress-queue.ts) has an undisclosed architectural defect that matters specifically because of this feature's target persona: it is a single global IndexedDB store scoped only to the browser origin, with no binding to the logged-in user/session and no clearing on logout or auth change. On a shared or handed-off field tablet -- the explicit, stated use case (siteSupervisor persona, construction-site connectivity) -- if Supervisor A queues entries offline and Supervisor B subsequently logs in on the same device before A's queue drains, WorkProgressClient's mount effect and the 'online' listener will auto-sync A's still-queued entries using B's active session (POST /api/work-progress infers organizationId/actor from requireAuth()'s server-side session context, not from any client-supplied field). This either misattributes A's progress data to B's account, or leaks A's queued entries (activity name, quantity, remarks, photo) into B's UI if the server rejects them as belonging to a different org. Separately, syncQueuedWorkProgressEntries() has no mutex against concurrent invocation -- overlapping calls from a remount plus a real-world duplicate 'online' event can both list the same pending entries before either flips status to 'syncing', risking duplicate POSTs of the same progress entry. Neither issue is covered by the new tests, which only exercise sequential, single-session sync. Given this is audit-trail data for an ERP feature and the target users are exactly the shared-device population most exposed to this bug, it should not merge as-is.
issues: src/lib/offline/work-progress-queue.ts: the queue is a single global IndexedDB store with no per-user/session scoping and nothing clears it on logout or account switch, so a second user logging into the same device can have the first user's queued (unsynced) work-progress entries auto-synced under their own session, or see the first user's queued entry data in their UI. Fix: scope the store key to the authenticated user/org, and clear or refuse to drain a queue whose entries don't match the current session on sync.

src/lib/offline/work-progress-queue.ts syncQueuedWorkProgressEntries(): no guard against concurrent execution -- overlapping calls (component remount racing the 'online' event, or a flaky connection firing multiple 'online' events) can both read the same pending entries before either is marked 'syncing', causing duplicate POST /api/work-progress calls for the same entry. Add an in-flight lock/dedupe.

Not a blocker but worth follow-up: failed sync entries (status 'error') retry forever on every 'online' event / manual sync with no backoff or max-attempt cap, so a permanently-invalid entry (e.g. its activityId was deleted server-side) will retry indefinitely.
